The Bad Creek Project would be part of the comprehensive development of the Keowee-Toxaway River Basin and was considered in the early planning stage of the Keowee-Toxaway Project. It would not require construction of a lower reservoir and, by operating in tandem with the existing Jocassee pumped storage project, would reduce present fluctuations of the Jocassee Reservoir.
A further impact of denying this application would be to deprive the Applicant and neighboring utilities of 1,000 megawatts of fast-response emergency peaking capacity in the event of system faults or outages. In addition, the 1,000 megavars of reactive power which the project could supply (for voltage correction, etc.) when operating as a synchronous condenser in the spinning-on-air mode would be lost to the Applicant's system.
If the application for license for this project is denied, the environment in the Bad Creek area would not be impacted as discussed earlier in this statement and would remain essentially as it is at present, with some possible changes as a result of logging and any other non-project activities which might take place in the area. Thirty-one miles of proposed hiking trail would also not be developed.
8.2.10 FEDERAL DEVELOPMENT
The pumped storage project has three important functions: (1) ability to store large blocks of energy produced by low-production cost fossil-fueled or nuclear generating units during off-peak hours so that the integrated system may obtain maximum benefit from the total capacity of high-efficiency units; (2) supplying energy during peak system demands at resultant costs which are less than the costs incurred when older steam-electric generating units, combustion turbines, or load-following steam units would otherwise be operated; (3) supplying reactive power when operated in the "spinning-in-air" mode.
These three functional characteristics dictate that the Bad Creek Project, to be economically and functionally feasible, must be part of a large electric generating system. The largest nearby Federal electric generating system is operated by the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA).
